mistIdeas: Our inference: make a short MIST interaction reel covering interruption, recognition, uncertainty and recovery, then approve those beats before expanding the expression library.
Our inference: judge whether the response reads with the mouth held still, so dialogue motion cannot hide weak acting.

title: Psychonauts 2: Richardson's mailroom robot acting

people.name: Miyuki Richardson
people.role: Animator in official credits; reel author showing in-game animations, layouts and cutscenes

summary: A credited animator's reel offers a useful robot comparison and clearly labels her animation work separately from layout-only contributions.

observations.text: In the inspected mailroom sequence around 4:08 to 4:20, the robot's luminous circular eye, head angle, and oversized mechanical hand make the letter exchange readable. At 4:14 the frame places the eye beside the envelope, bringing face and task into one composition.

At approximately 4:20 the reel visibly labels the shot 'Layout and Animation'. Earlier examples, including the inspected 1:36 frame, say 'Layout Only' and credit final animation to Squeeze Animation Studios.
Double Fine's official credits name Richardson among the animators and separately acknowledge FaceFX-generated facial animations; this does not establish which mechanism any individual shot uses.

mistIdeas: Our inference: tie a MIST attention change to an actual event or object, then align the face, head, and one body gesture around that target.
Our inference: a mechanical face can retain its identity while the head and body carry emphasis. Avoid forcing a human mouth performance into every response.
Our inference: review future MIST animation in labelled stages: anticipation, attention shift, reaction hold, and return. The reel does not supply measured timing values for these stages.

title: Spiritfarer: individuality within a shared action set
summary: The animators explain how common actions can carry distinct personalities, a useful foundation for MIST's event-driven reactions.

observations.text: Boyer and Pelletier describe a largely shared action list for the spirits, including interaction, eating, sleeping and hugging, while making each spirit's movement individual.

The interview identifies dialogue expressions among Stella's animation work. It also describes returning control once an action has communicated its meaning, allowing the player to cancel into another action.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give MIST a common reaction structure with expression-specific gaze, eyelids and recovery, rather than using the same bounce for every event.

Our inference: define the minimum visible beat of a reaction and let a new conversational event interrupt its tail. Preserve the emotional eye pose when speech begins instead of resetting the face to neutral.

title: Thank Goodness You're Here!: Pip Williamson's hybrid character workflow

people.name: Pip Williamson
people.role: Animation team lead; character, interactive and stylised animation

summary: A named animation lead explains how to preserve drawn poses when implementing character animation in an engine.

observations.text: Pip says the team began with free-drawn roughs, then used a hybrid workflow combining in-engine animation and replacement sprites where position, rotation and scale were insufficient.
Her portfolio says this retained snappy movements from the frame-by-frame roughs, and identifies her work animating over 200 game elements and leading the animation team.

mistIdeas: Our inference: sketch MIST's extreme mouth and eyelid poses first, then decide which transitions need replacement drawings. Do not force every expression through interpolation of one neutral shape.
Our inference: compare rough expression changes against the final engine playback so implementation convenience does not erase the pose contrast.

title: Wirm: a minimal face reacts to falling

people.name: Riley Neville
people.role: Developer; describes making Wirm in a direct 2022 interview

summary: A useful indie comparator because its creator explicitly ties a tiny facial change to a physical event: falling off a rock.

observations.text: Neville describes Wirm's smiling face changing to an open-mouth expression when it falls off a rock. This is direct evidence of an event-driven expression rather than a claim inferred from a trailer.
The inspected official screenshot shows only small dark face marks at the worm's end, while the body drapes over a rock toward a gap. The facial marks remain attached to the body's orientation.

mistIdeas: Our inference: connect surprise to a real interrupt or unexpected outcome, then let the face recover when that condition ends.

Our inference: test the same causal structure with MIST's eyes alone: a brief opening change followed by a stable look at the cause. The mouth is optional; the event relationship is the useful reference.
Our inference: a blink can punctuate the return to listening after surprise, but the sources here do not establish a Wirm blink technique.
